questions.q: What did Western Orientalists do with knowledge about the East?
a: Used it to justify political and economic control
Shared it freely with Eastern scholars
Preserved it without any political purpose
Rejected it in favor of local accounts
questions.why: Lesson 1 says studying the Orient became a means of political and economic gain for the West.

questions.q: What happened to diversity within Eastern nations under Orientalist categories?
a: It was lost as people were lumped into broad groups
It was carefully documented and celebrated
It became the main focus of study
It was protected by colonial laws
questions.why: Lesson 2 says broad categories erased the diversity of individuals within Eastern nations.

questions.q: Why was Napoleon's Egyptian expedition significant?
a: It included scholars who served French interests
It ended all trade between Egypt and France
It was a purely scientific mission
It introduced Arabic science to Europe
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Napoleon's expedition bringing scholars who protected French trade interests.

questions.q: Where does the summary say Orientalism still appears today?
a: Popular imagination, universities and government policy
Museums, courts and sporting events
Advertising, fashion and popular music
Schools, hospitals and charitable groups
questions.why: Lesson 3 names popular imagination, universities and government policies as places Orientalism survives.

questions.q: How did the 1973 oil crisis shape images of Arabs in the West?
a: Cartoons cast Arabs as villains near oil pumps
It created widespread sympathy for Arab nations
It led to more accurate portrayals in the media
It ended the use of stereotypes in cartoons
questions.why: Lesson 3 links the 1973 oil crisis to cartoons of Arab sheiks that cast the East as villain.
